<reason>Both sides were sharp, aphoristic, and stayed on the motion as written. B built the cleaner decision structure: a dilemma (value-producing = job; observational = carved out), an equity filter argument, and — decisively — the exploitation of A's own concession that the placement "only makes sense if cash is not also required," reframed as a wage subsidy funded by family wealth. B then honestly conceded A's central scarcity claim ("often, yes, a deleted slot") and weighed it away with the strongest line of the debate: volume rationed by private income is "zero, printed a hundred times." That is a real answer to A's best route rather than an evasion. A's best work was regulatory-design pressure: that a heavy rule will be written as a checklist, and that B's own non-substitution criterion reimports the binary and swallows mixed placements ("the carve-out is theatre"). That landed and kept the margin competitive. A also correctly noted that not every unpaid slot is a three-month capital relocation, and that restriction may push privilege off the books into nephew-style favours. But A's counterplan (stipends/travel grants) was partly absorbed by B's "take both — fund it once you stop subsidising employers," and A never squarely rebutted the core claim that the unconnected applicant could not have accepted the deleted slot in the first place, relying instead on late assertions about short, local, home-based placements. Pressure questions were pointed on both sides and both answered with proper A1:/A2: labelling. Both openings were clipped for length, an equal execution cost. B made the choice easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's turning of A's concession in [A2.7] — that the placement "only makes sense if cash is not also required" — into proof that the model's viability depends on family wealth, then carrying it into the closing as the single sentence to decide on. A's counter that this is merely the condition allowing a small office to host anyone was plausible but never fully escaped the wealth-filter inference.</best_rebuttal>
